name: Subagent Workflow
description: Wire coding-agent harnesses into a workflow on a canvas: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, opencode, Aider, Cursor Agent, the built-in Pi runner, or a custom command. Bookend it with start and end nodes, drop in human approval gates, and give each node three things — its provider, its model and its user message — from the gear on the node, which opens its full-screen settings over the canvas, then run the whole graph server-side and watch every node stream its output. The **messages sidebar** beside the canvas lists what every agent actually said: click an agent to read that one agent's messages, a waiting gate to see the input each agent wired into it produced together with its own Approve / Reject buttons, or the end node to read the workflow's final output split into a section per agent. A Pi node picks from every model this app can run, grouped by provider (`provider/model`), and reference **files and folders** — typed, or picked from a browser of the workspace — are injected into a node's message with their paths and descriptions. The wiring decides the order: nodes connected in parallel run in parallel, a chain runs one after another, and the start and end nodes take as many connections as you draw. Runs can start on a schedule or on observed events, and every past run stays in the workspace's history to reopen. Each harness's binary can be pointed at by hand from the plugin's ⚙ Settings in Settings → Plugins, so a CLI installed outside the PATH a desktop launch resolves (an nvm or npm-global prefix, a custom location) is found, validated and run — and any CLI of your own can be defined there by name and binary, with an argument template and the models it offers, which then appear in every node's Provider and Model lists.
author: Pi Scope
